source.author_body: Hi IH, I'm Vadym and I'm building Upperdoc in public. The problem that got me started: small firms send a client a list of documents, half come back, and then someone spends the next two weeks writing polite follow-up emails. It's not hard work, it's just endless. So Upperdoc does one thing. You create a request with a checklist, send the client one branded link, and they upload straight from it. No account, no password. Reminders go out on their own at 3, 7 and 14 days until the checklist is complete, and a green/amber/red dashboard shows what's still missing per client. There's optional AI that checks uploads against what you asked for, but it only suggests. It never approves or rejects anything by itself. That felt important for people who are professionally responsible for the paperwork. It's early access: self-serve signup and a 14-day trial work, no paying customers yet. My question for accountants and bookkeepers here: how do you chase documents today? Email threads, a portal from your practice software, a spreadsheet? And what makes clients actually upload on time? https://upperdoc.io

metadata.headline: Accountants spend weeks chasing client documents. I'm trying to make that boring

source.decision: Discussion/seller/product research only; no paid buyer or complete competition/contact evidence
